questions.question: Recognize the link between passenger satisfaction and repeat travel. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Recognize the link between passenger satisfaction and repeat travel.
  • Passenger satisfaction plays a crucial role in influencing repeat travel decisions in the airline industry.
  • When passengers receive high-quality inflight food service, courteous behavior from cabin crew, and
  • timely service, they develop a positive perception of the airline. This satisfaction builds trust and loyalty,
  • encouraging passengers to choose the same airline for future journeys. Consistency in service quality
  • further strengthens this relationship. On the other hand, poor service can lead to dissatisfaction and loss of
  • customers. Therefore, maintaining high standards in inflight food service directly contributes to customer
  • retention and repeat business.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Identify the food service standard followed by full-service airlines. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Identify the food service standard followed by full-service airlines.
  • Full-service airlines follow a high standard of food service that includes complimentary meals, beverages,
  • and a variety of menu options tailored to passenger preferences. These airlines emphasize quality,
  • hygiene, and presentation, often offering multi-course meals on long-haul flights. Special meals such as
  • vegetarian, diabetic, or religious meals are also provided upon request. The service includes proper table
  • settings, use of standard recipes, and trained cabin crew ensuring professional delivery. Overall, the aim is
  • to enhance passenger comfort and provide a premium travel experience.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the significance of correct storage and handling of inflight food service equipment. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the significance of correct storage and handling of inflight food service equipment. Correct
  • storage and handling of inflight food service equipment are essential to maintain hygiene, safety, and
  • efficiency. Equipment such as meal carts, trays, and utensils must be stored in clean, dry, and designated
  • areas to prevent contamination. Proper handling ensures that the equipment remains in good condition,
  • reducing the risk of damage or malfunction during service. It also helps in maintaining food quality by
  • preventing cross-contamination. Following standard procedures for cleaning and storage enhances
  • operational efficiency and ensures compliance with safety regulations.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the importance of regular maintenance of inflight food service equipment. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the importance of regular maintenance of inflight food service equipment.
  • Regular maintenance of inflight food service equipment is vital to ensure smooth and safe operations
  • during flights. Equipment like ovens, refrigerators, and meal carts must function properly to maintain
  • food quality and service efficiency. Routine checks help identify faults early, preventing unexpected
  • breakdowns that could disrupt service. Maintenance also ensures compliance with safety and hygiene
  • standards, reducing the risk of contamination or accidents. Well-maintained equipment improves
  • reliability, extends lifespan, and supports consistent service delivery.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Classify the different types of special meals planned for diverse passenger needs in inflight service. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Classify the different types of special meals planned for diverse passenger needs in inflight service.
  • Special meals in inflight service are classified based on medical, religious, and lifestyle requirements.
  • Medical meals include diabetic, low-sodium, gluten-free, and low-fat meals designed to meet health
  • needs. Religious meals include halal, kosher, and Hindu meals, prepared according to specific cultural
  • practices. Lifestyle meals include vegetarian, vegan, and child meals, catering to personal preferences.
  • There are also infant meals and meals for passengers with allergies. Proper classification helps airlines
  • meet diverse passenger expectations and ensures comfort and satisfaction during travel.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the responsibilities of cabin crew during food-related emergencies. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the responsibilities of cabin crew during food-related emergencies.
  • During food-related emergencies, cabin crew have the responsibility to respond quickly and effectively to
  • ensure passenger safety. They must identify symptoms such as allergic reactions, choking, or food
  • poisoning and provide immediate assistance. Crew members are trained in first aid and may use onboard
  • medical kits or seek help from medical professionals among passengers. They must communicate clearly
  • with the cockpit crew and follow emergency protocols. Proper documentation and reporting of the
  • incident are also essential. Their prompt action can prevent serious health complications.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Summarize the role of temperature control in ensuring inflight food quality. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Summarize the role of temperature control in ensuring inflight food quality.
  • Temperature control is a critical factor in maintaining inflight food quality and safety. Food must be
  • stored, transported, and reheated at appropriate temperatures to prevent microbial growth and spoilage.
  • Cold foods should be kept chilled, while hot foods must be reheated to safe serving temperatures.
  • Maintaining the correct temperature preserves taste, texture, and nutritional value. It also ensures
  • compliance with food safety standards and reduces the risk of foodborne illnesses. Effective temperature
  • control systems are essential for delivering safe and high-quality meals to passengers.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Interpret the importance of standard recipes in menu cost control. / [CO4] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Interpret the importance of standard recipes in menu cost control.
  • Standard recipes play a key role in controlling menu costs in airline catering. They ensure consistency in
  • ingredient quantities, portion sizes, and preparation methods, which helps in accurate cost estimation. By
  • minimizing wastage and avoiding overuse of ingredients, standard recipes contribute to efficient resource
  • utilization. They also support inventory management and budgeting by providing clear guidelines for
  • procurement. Consistency in recipes ensures uniform quality across flights, enhancing passenger
  • satisfaction while maintaining cost efficiency.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Examine common equipment malfunctions affecting inflight food service and discuss preventive measures. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Examine common equipment malfunctions affecting inflight food service and discuss preventive
  • measures.
  • Inflight food service depends heavily on the proper functioning of various equipment such as ovens,
  • refrigerators, beverage makers, and meal carts. Common malfunctions include oven heating failures,
  • refrigeration breakdowns, electrical faults, and mechanical issues in meal carts. These problems can lead
  • to improper heating or storage of food, affecting both food safety and service efficiency. For example, a
  • faulty refrigerator may cause food spoilage, while a malfunctioning oven may prevent proper reheating of
  • meals. Preventive measures include regular inspection, scheduled maintenance, and proper handling of
  • equipment. Cabin crew should be trained to identify early signs of malfunction and report them
  • immediately. Pre-flight checks, adherence to maintenance schedules, and proper cleaning practices also
  • help reduce equipment failures. Ensuring backup systems and contingency planning further supports
  • uninterrupted service.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the concept of special meals in inflight food service and discuss their significance for passenger safety and satisfaction. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the concept of special meals in inflight food service and discuss their significance for
  • passenger safety and satisfaction.
  • Special meals in inflight food service are customized meals prepared to meet the specific dietary, medical,
  • religious, or lifestyle requirements of passengers. These include diabetic meals, low-sodium meals,
  • gluten-free meals, halal, kosher, vegetarian, vegan, and infant meals. The concept is based on providing
  • inclusive service that accommodates diverse passenger needs. The significance of special meals lies in
  • ensuring passenger safety, particularly for those with allergies or medical conditions, as inappropriate
  • food can lead to serious health issues. Additionally, offering culturally and religiously appropriate meals
  • enhances passenger comfort and satisfaction. It reflects the airline’s commitment to quality service and
  • customer care. Proper labeling, handling, and timely delivery of special meals are essential to maintain
  • trust and prevent errors. Overall, special meals contribute to a positive travel experience and customer
  • loyalty.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the role of cabin crew in maintaining service quality, safety, and passenger satisfaction during inflight meal service. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role of cabin crew in maintaining service quality, safety, and passenger satisfaction
  • during inflight meal service.
  • Cabin crew play a vital role in ensuring high standards of service quality, safety, and passenger
  • satisfaction during inflight meal service. They are responsible for the proper handling, reheating, and
  • distribution of meals according to established procedures. Maintaining hygiene and food safety is a key
  • duty, including the use of protective clothing and adherence to sanitation standards. Cabin crew also
  • ensure that passengers receive the correct meals, especially in the case of special dietary requirements.
  • Effective communication, courteous behavior, and prompt service enhance the overall passenger
  • experience. In addition, crew members must monitor passengers for any food-related issues such as
  • allergies or discomfort and respond appropriately. Their professionalism, efficiency, and attention to
  • detail significantly influence passenger satisfaction and the airline’s reputation.

questions.question: Discuss the planning and preparation of inflight menus with reference to passenger needs and flight duration. / [CO2] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the planning and preparation of inflight menus with reference to passenger needs and flight
  • duration.
  • Planning and preparation of inflight menus is a complex process that considers passenger needs, flight
  • duration, route, and operational constraints. For short-haul flights, menus are usually simple, including
  • light snacks and beverages, while long-haul flights require more elaborate multi-course meals. Passenger
  • needs such as cultural preferences, dietary restrictions, age groups, and health conditions must be taken
  • into account. Menu planning also involves balancing nutrition, taste, and presentation while ensuring food
  • safety and quality. Factors such as limited storage space, reheating facilities, and changes in taste
  • perception at high altitude must be considered. Standard recipes and portion control are used to maintain
  • consistency and cost efficiency. Coordination with ground catering services is essential for timely
  • preparation and delivery of meals. Proper packaging, labeling, and temperature control are crucial to
  • preserve food quality. Overall, effective menu planning enhances passenger satisfaction and ensures a
  • smooth inflight service experience.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
